lanes.subtitle: twelve fires, in the order the chart keeps them

stations.place: the sky over the first sea
stations.title: THE FIRST FIRE
stations.claim: The Chronicon starts its count 1,344 years before Year One: 5239 BC, a fire crossing the sky, the first year anyone counted from.
stations.anchor: 5239 − 3895 = 1,344. From 5239 BC to 2106 AD is 7,344 years with no year zero: 5239 + 2106 − 1.
stations.check: 5239 BC is the start of Breshears' Anunnaki reckoning (Chronicon); no dated sky event survives in any archaeological or textual record for that year. The arithmetic holds.
stations.natori: Fifty-two thirty-nine BC. Something crossed the sky, and somebody started counting.
stations.rogue: Thirteen hundred forty-four years before Year One. Seven thousand three hundred forty-four to the capstone.

stations.title: SHADOW ENTERS THE CIRCLE
stations.claim: The chart starts the chronoliths, the standing-stone clocks, in 4309 BC, the first year a shadow entered a circle's centre on purpose.
stations.anchor: 5239 − 4309 = 930, the years of Adam's life in Genesis 5:5. A stone's shadow reaches a circle's centre only at one fixed date each year.
stations.fact: 5239 − 4309 = 930, the years of Adam's life in Genesis 5:5.
stations.check: No dated stone circle is that old: Göbekli Tepe's enclosures are c. 9500 BC, Stonehenge's sarsens c. 2500 BC. 4309 BC is the chart's date; 930 is Genesis 5:5.
stations.natori: Forty-three oh nine. The first shadow to cross a circle's centre on purpose.
stations.rogue: Nine hundred thirty years after the first fire. Adam's whole life, to the year.

stations.title: YEAR ONE
stations.claim: Year One. The gate of Eden closes behind two people walking out onto the ash, and the Anno Mundi count begins.
stations.anchor: 3895 BC is Anno Mundi 1 in the Chronicon, and AD = AM − 3894 (AM 5796 = 1902). Ussher's creation is 4004 BC; the Hebrew calendar's is 3761 BC.
stations.fact: 3895 BC is Anno Mundi 1, and AD = AM − 3894. Ussher says 4004 BC; the Hebrew calendar, 3761.
stations.check: Three creations, none archaeological: Ussher 4004 BC, the Hebrew calendar 3761 BC, Breshears 3895 BC. Only the last one puts 1902 on a 138-multiple.
stations.natori: Thirty-eight ninety-five. Year One. The gate closes and the counting starts.
stations.rogue: Two people, one road, and a number that never stops.

stations.title: THE ARCS
stations.claim: The cipher draws the same span on both sides of a date: from the Flood, 792 and 1,200 years either way, and something lands at each end.
stations.anchor: 2239 − 792 = 1447 BC, the early Exodus date. 2239 + 1200 = 3439 BC. Both spans are struck from AM 1656.
stations.fact: 2239 − 792 = 1447 BC, the early Exodus. 2239 + 1200 = 3439 BC. Both struck from AM 1656.
stations.check: 1447 BC is the traditional early Exodus (1 Kings 6:1); many scholars prefer the 13th century BC. 3439 BC is Breshears' catastrophe date, unrecorded elsewhere. The 792 and 1,200 spans are the chart's.
stations.natori: Every date has a mirror. Seven hundred ninety-two years one way, seven ninety-two the other.
stations.rogue: Twelve hundred does it too. The line doesn't care which way you walk it.

stations.title: THE HINGE
stations.claim: The Flood sits exactly 1,656 years after Year One and exactly 1,656 years before the Medo-Lydian eclipse. Natori threads the two.
stations.check: AM 1656 for the Flood is the Masoretic sum; the Septuagint gives 2242. Thales' eclipse is astronomically 28 May 585 BC, two years off the chart's 583. The subtraction holds.
stations.natori: Sixteen fifty-six years in. Sixteen fifty-six years out. The Flood is the hinge.
stations.rogue: Eden on one side, Thales on the other. Twelve fires each way.

stations.title: THE RAIN BEGINS
stations.claim: The Flood begins as rain on a stone plain while a pale wall of water rises along the whole horizon, and two people watch it come.
stations.anchor: Genesis 7:11–12: the fountains of the deep and the windows of heaven, forty days of rain. AM 1656 = 138 × 12, the twelfth Phoenix.
stations.fact: Genesis 7:11–12: forty days of rain. AM 1656 = 138 × 12, the twelfth Phoenix.
stations.check: No global flood layer exists in the geological record; the Mesopotamian flood deposits at Ur, Kish and Shuruppak date c. 2900 BC and are local. The year is the Chronicon's.
stations.natori: Twenty-two thirty-nine. The rain comes first. The water is already on its way.
stations.rogue: Twelfth fire. Every fourth one is a flood. This is the first.

stations.title: THE SUSPENDED SEA
stations.claim: The wave stops mid-fall. The chart reads the Flood as the exact centre of a mirror: what came before it returns after it.
stations.anchor: Played forward then backward, the six-second wave is its own palindrome. AM 1656 is one of only 43 years in six thousand that sit on a 138-multiple.
stations.fact: AM 1656 is one of only 43 years in six thousand that sit on a multiple of 138.
stations.check: The Flood as a chronological axis is the chart's reading; Genesis gives the Flood a year and ten days (7:11 to 8:14), not a moment. The 43-of-6,000 count is arithmetic.
stations.natori: Hold it there. Halfway between the gate and the eclipse.
stations.rogue: A suspended sea. It reads the same falling or rising.

stations.title: THE RAIN ENDS
stations.claim: The last rain thins, the water draws back to a silver line on the horizon, and a band of gold opens under the cloud.
stations.anchor: Genesis 8:14: the earth was dry in Noah's 601st year, on the 27th day of the second month — 370 days after the rain began.
stations.fact: Genesis 8:14: the earth was dry 370 days after the rain began.
stations.check: 370 days is the Masoretic count (7:11 to 8:14); the Septuagint and Samaritan texts run other Flood calendars. The gold band under the cloud is the film's, not the text's.
stations.natori: The water goes back the way it came. It always does.
stations.rogue: Three hundred seventy days, if you count the way Genesis counts.

stations.title: FOUR PULSES
stations.claim: A comet's glow crosses a darkened sun and Natori counts four pulses at her throat: four fires since the Flood, and the sea over Attica.
stations.anchor: AM 2208 = 138 × 16. 2239 − 1687 = 552 = 138 × 4. The Flood of Ogyges is the chart's sixteenth Phoenix and the second link of the flood chain.
stations.fact: AM 2208 = 138 × 16. 2239 − 1687 = 552 = 138 × 4: the second link of the flood chain.
stations.check: Ogyges' flood is dated by Julius Africanus c. 1796 BC and by Varro c. 1600 BC; no comet is recorded. The shot's caption reads 1688; AM 2208 is 1687 BC by the Chronicon rule.
stations.natori: Sixteen eighty-seven. Ogyges. Four pulses, four fires, one flood.
stations.rogue: Five hundred fifty-two years. The second link of the chain.

stations.title: THE ECLIPSE BATTLE
stations.claim: The sun goes out over the Halys; Medes and Lydians lower their spears and the war ends where it stands. Thales had called it.
stations.anchor: AM 3312 = 138 × 24. Herodotus I.74: day became night in mid-battle and both sides made peace. Astronomers place the eclipse on 28 May 585 BC.
stations.fact: AM 3312 = 138 × 24. Herodotus I.74: day became night mid-battle. Astronomers say 28 May 585 BC.
stations.check: The Halys eclipse is 585 BC by retrocalculation; the chart's 583 BC is AM 3312 by arithmetic, two years off. Herodotus is the only ancient source for the prediction.
stations.natori: Five eighty-three. The sun went out and the war stopped where it stood.
stations.rogue: Twenty-fourth fire. Thales called it. The book rounds two years. Note it.

stations.title: SHADOW LEAVES THE CIRCLE
stations.claim: The chronoliths end: the shadow slides out of the circle's centre as a steam train's smoke crosses the field. 1902, the Red Mud Event.
stations.anchor: AM 5796 = 138 × 42. On 8 May 1902 Mont Pelée destroyed Saint-Pierre, Martinique, in minutes. 1902 + 138 = 2040.
stations.fact: AM 5796 = 138 × 42. 8 May 1902: Mont Pelée destroys Saint-Pierre. 1902 + 138 = 2040.
stations.check: Mont Pelée, 8 May 1902, about 28,000 dead, is on every record; "red mud" as the year's signature is the chart's reading. The chronolith window (4309 BC to 1902 AD) is Breshears'.
stations.natori: Nineteen oh two. The shadow leaves the circle. The stones stop keeping time.
stations.rogue: Forty-second fire. Red mud in the rain. One left before the one she hasn't seen.

stations.title: FIRE AGAIN
stations.claim: The projected one: a burning streak over a lit coastline. The chart says the next fire is due, and the Codex gives it a margin.
stations.anchor: 1902 + 138 = 2040 = AM 5934 = 138 × 43. The Codex's Chronologist: "as early as 2039, as late as 2046 for the worst of it."
stations.fact: 1902 + 138 = 2040 = AM 5934 = 138 × 43. The Codex: "as early as 2039, as late as 2046."
stations.check: 2040 is arithmetic on the chart; 2046 is the Codex's margin, not a Long Count date — the 13th baktun ended 21 December 2012. Nothing in this station is on any record yet.
stations.natori: Twenty forty. Or twenty forty-six. The one she hasn't seen.
stations.rogue: One thirty-eight from nineteen oh two. Same sky as the first frame.
